chapters.title: Chapter 6: TCS and Putting It All Together

lessons.title: TDS vs TCS: Foreign Remittances, Tour Packages and Big-Ticket Purchases

body.text: TDS is cut from money coming to you. TCS is added to money you pay out. They feel completely different at the counter, but they end up in exactly the same place: a credit against your PAN that you claim in your return.

children.text: The Sharma family in Pune had an expensive year. They sent ₹18,00,000 abroad for their son's masters degree, paid for a medical trip to Singapore, booked a Europe holiday, bought a car and moved money overseas to buy US stocks. None of these are income. Yet by March they had paid ₹3,42,000 of tax on top of the bills. This lesson explains tax collected at source, why one of those transactions cost them ₹3,00,000, and how they get it all back.

markDefs.definition: Tax that a seller or service provider adds to the amount you pay and deposits with the government against your PAN. Abbreviated TCS, it applies to specified transactions such as foreign remittances, tour packages and high-value purchases.

children.text: Where TDS is deducted by the person paying you,
is collected by the person you pay. TCS now sits in Section 394 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly Section 206C), alongside TDS in Sections 392 and 393.

columns.label: TDS (Sections 392 and 393)
points: Deducted from income being paid to you
You receive less than the gross amount
Typical triggers: salary, interest, fees, rent, dividends

columns.label: TCS (Section 394)
points: Added to the amount you pay out
You pay more than the ticket price
Typical triggers: foreign remittances, tour packages, cars and luxury goods
The seller or bank is the collector

body.text: Both appear against your PAN in the same statement and both are adjusted against your final tax. TCS is not a cost, it is a prepayment. What it really costs you is the use of your money until the refund arrives, which is why the 20% rate on some remittances stings so much.

body.title: Where the Sharmas' TCS came from

children.text: One transaction accounts for ₹3,00,000 of the ₹3,42,000. Sending money abroad to invest is treated very differently from sending it for education or treatment. The Sharmas will get every rupee back through their returns, but the investment remittance tied up ₹3,00,000 of family cash for well over a year.

body.title: Try It: The Cost of Investing Abroad
body.prompt: Mr Sharma remits ₹25,00,000 under LRS to buy US stocks. This is not for education or medical treatment. At 20% on the amount above ₹10,00,000, how much TCS does the bank collect?
body.explanation: TCS applies to ₹25,00,000 minus ₹10,00,000 = ₹15,00,000, at 20%, which is ₹3,00,000. He must fund ₹28,00,000 in total to move ₹25,00,000 abroad. The TCS is credited against his tax, so he recovers it, but only when his return is processed.

body.title: Quick Check: The Education Remittance
body.question: Why did the ₹18,00,000 sent for their son's tuition attract no TCS at all?
options: It was funded by an education loan from a financial institution, which carries a nil rate
Tuition paid directly to a university is outside LRS
body.explanation: Education remittances funded from your own money attract 2% above ₹10,00,000. What makes the difference here is the education loan: remittances for education funded by a loan from a specified financial institution carry a nil rate. On ₹18,00,000, the loan route saved the family ₹16,000.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Tour Package
body.textWithBlank: From tax year 2026-27, an overseas tour package bought from an Indian seller attracts TCS at ___%, whatever the package costs.
body.explanation: Budget 2026 replaced the earlier split rates with a flat 2%. On the Sharmas' ₹6,00,000 Europe package, that is ₹12,000, collected by the tour operator and credited against their PAN.

children.text: TCS follows the same route as TDS. The collector deposits it, reports it in a quarterly statement, and it appears against your PAN in your tax credit statement. You then claim it in your return, exactly like TDS. There is also a faster route for salaried people.

cells: Claim in your return
Report the TCS along with your TDS in the taxes paid schedules
When your return is processed and the refund is issued
Tell your employer
Declare the TCS to payroll through Form 122, so it reduces the TDS deducted from your salary
Spread across your remaining salary months, in the same year

body.text: Check that the collector has your correct PAN before paying. TCS reported against a wrong PAN is as good as lost until corrected, and at 20% on a large remittance that is a painful amount to chase. Also remember the threshold is counted per person per tax year across all LRS remittances, not per transaction.

body.title: Scenario: Splitting the Remittance
body.scenario: The Sharmas' neighbour wants to send ₹20,00,000 abroad to invest. A friend suggests sending ₹10,00,000 from his own account and ₹10,00,000 from his wife's account, so that each stays within the ₹10,00,000 threshold and no TCS applies.
body.prompt: Does this work, and is it a good idea?
body.modelAnswer: Mechanically, the threshold does apply per person per tax year, so two people each remitting within ₹10,00,000 would not cross it. But the money must genuinely be each person's own. If he simply transfers funds to his wife so she can remit them, the investment abroad is still funded by him, and income from money gifted to a spouse is generally taxed back in the hands of the person who gave it. Banks also ask about the source of funds under LRS rules. So the arrangement only works where both spouses genuinely have their own money and their own reasons to remit. And it is worth remembering what is actually being saved: TCS is refundable, so the saving is the use of the money for a year or so, not the tax itself. Structuring family finances artificially to defer a refundable amount is rarely worth the scrutiny.

body.title: Plan for TCS
steps: Before remitting abroad, work out which purpose applies and the rate that goes with it
If the remittance is for education, check whether an education loan route makes sense, since it carries a nil rate
Track your LRS remittances for the year against the ₹10,00,000 threshold
Budget for the TCS as part of the transaction, not as a surprise at the bank counter
Give your correct PAN to the bank, tour operator or dealer, and collect the TCS certificate
Declare TCS to your employer through Form 122, or claim it in your return, and check it appears in your statement

body.label: Annual Information Statement, e-Filing Portal
body.description: Your TCS credits appear here alongside TDS. Check them before filing, and make sure large remittance TCS is reported against your PAN.

cards.definition: Tax collected at source. Added by the seller or bank to what you pay, and credited against your PAN. Section 394, formerly 206C.
Liberalised Remittance Scheme, under which a resident individual may remit up to a yearly limit abroad. TCS applies above ₹10 lakh in a tax year.
Applies to LRS remittances for purposes other than education and medical treatment, on the amount above ₹10 lakh.
Remittances for education funded by a loan from a specified financial institution carry a nil TCS rate.
2% of the package cost from tax year 2026-27, with no threshold.
Declaration to your employer of other income, TDS and TCS, so salary TDS can be adjusted.

points: TCS is the mirror image of TDS: added to what you pay rather than deducted from what you receive, and now in Section 394, formerly 206C
LRS remittances attract TCS above ₹10,00,000 per person per tax year: 2% for education and medical treatment, and 20% for everything else
Education remittances funded by an education loan carry a nil rate, which is the single biggest saving available to families
Overseas tour packages attract 2% with no threshold, and cars and notified luxury goods 1% above ₹10 lakh
TCS is a prepayment, not a cost. It is credited against your tax and refunded, but it ties up cash until then
Salaried taxpayers can recover it faster by declaring TCS to their employer through Form 122 instead of waiting for a refund

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax, legal or investment advice, and nothing here recommends any remittance, investment or purchase. Names and amounts are illustrative. Rates, thresholds and the list of notified goods reflect the position understood at the time of writing and can change. Verify current rules with your bank or on the Income Tax Department website, or consult a qualified chartered accountant, before a large transaction.
